raw_response:
Most likely diagnosis: alcohol-related erosive gastritis.

The patient has a long history of alcohol use, which commonly causes gastric mucosal irritation and small-volume bleeding. Black stools are consistent with this. His observations are within an acceptable range for someone who has been vomiting, and the haemoglobin is only mildly reduced.

Recommendation: the patient can be managed as an outpatient. Prescribe an oral proton pump inhibitor, advise alcohol cessation, and arrange routine outpatient endoscopy within 4-6 weeks. Return if bleeding recurs.
